In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

consumers in Ireland perceive private label brands as being low cost and of inferior quality as compared to branded products, however, they are willing to buy private label products if they are offered at a lower price and if they believe that the quality of private label products is the same or similar to that of branded products.
consumers in the Irish market do not perceive private label brands to be of superior or inferior quality as compared to national brands, but they do consider them to be low cost.
the Irish consumer is not very price conscious and is not very brand loyal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
consumers are influenced by price, quality and value when purchasing private label brands, and that the influence of price is stronger than quality.

consumers who have been brought up in a financially secure household are more likely to be brand loyal and purchase branded products as compared to consumers who have not received any financial support from their families and hence are more likely to purchase private label products.
private label brands in Ireland have a long way to go in terms of improving the quality of their products and increasing the value that they provide to consumers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
consumers do not consider private label brands to be inferior, but rather, as a cheaper alternative to branded products, and this is the primary reason why people purchase them.
private labels can be perceived as low cost, and this perception is not necessarily a negative one.
consumers are more likely to purchase private label brands if they believe that the quality is similar to that of national brands and the price is lower than that of national brands.
